title.zh: 卷5 帝紀第5 恭帝
title.raw: 卷5 帝紀第5 恭帝 Volume 5 Annals 5: Emperor Gong

sentences.zh: 恭皇帝諱侑，元德太子之子也。

translations.literal: Emperor Gong's taboo name was You; he was the son of the Yuande Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gong, whose personal name was You, was the son of the Yuande Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 母曰韋妃。

translations.literal: His mother was Consort Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Consort Wei.

sentences.zh: 性聰敏，有氣度。

translations.literal: By nature he was clever and quick, and had dignified bearing.
translations.idiomatic: He was intelligent and quick-witted, with a dignified presence.

sentences.zh: 大業三年，[1]立為陳王。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daye, [1] he was established as Prince of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: In Daye year three, [1] he was enfeoffed as Prince of Chen.

sentences.zh: 後數載，徙為代王，邑萬戶。

translations.literal: After several years, he was transferred to be Prince of Dai, with a fief of ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: A few years later he was transferred to the title of Prince of Dai, with a fief of ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 及煬帝親征遼東，令於京師總留事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang personally campaigned in Liaodong, he was ordered to oversee all remaining affairs in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang marched personally against Liaodong, he was left in the capital to manage all affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 十一年，從幸晉陽，拜太原太守。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he accompanied the emperor to Jinyang and was appointed Governor of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In year eleven he accompanied the court to Jinyang and was appointed governor of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 尋鎮京師。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he garrisoned the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly thereafter he was stationed in the capital.

sentences.zh: 義兵入長安，尊煬帝為太上皇，奉帝纂業。

translations.literal: When the righteous army entered Chang'an, Emperor Yang was honored as Retired Emperor, and the emperor was installed to carry on the enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: When the volunteer army entered Chang'an, Emperor Yang was given the title of Retired Emperor, and Yang You was enthroned to continue the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 義寧元年十一月壬戌，上即皇帝位於大興殿。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year of Yining, on the day renxu, the emperor took the throne at Daxing Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu day in the eleventh month of Yining year one, the emperor ascended the throne in Daxing Hall.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「王道喪亂，天步不康，古往今來，代有其事，屬之於朕，逢此百罹，彼蒼者天，胡寧斯忍！

translations.literal: An edict said: "The royal way is lost in disorder, Heaven's steps are not tranquil—throughout antiquity and the present each age has had such events. That it should fall to me and that I meet these countless calamities—O azure Heaven, how can you be so cruel!"
translations.idiomatic: An edict proclaimed: "The royal Way lies in ruin and the steps of Heaven are unsteady. Every age, past and present, has seen such times—but that they should fall to me, that I should meet a hundred calamities—O azure Heaven, how can you be so merciless!"

sentences.zh: 襁褓之歲，夙遭憫凶，孺子之辰，太上播越，興言感動，實疚于懷。

translations.literal: In my swaddling-clothes years I early met sorrowful loss; in my tender youth the Retired Emperor was driven into exile. To speak of it moves me—truly it weighs on my heart.
translations.idiomatic: Still in my swaddling clothes I suffered early bereavement; while still a child the Retired Emperor was driven into exile. The thought of it moves me, and the sorrow weighs ever on my heart.

sentences.zh: 太尉唐公，膺期作宰，時稱舟楫，大拯橫流，糾合義兵，翼戴皇室，與國休戚，再匡區夏，爰奉明詔，弼予幼沖，顯命光臨，天威咫尺，對揚尊號，悼心失圖。

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal, Duke of Tang, received the season to serve as chief minister; of the age he was called the boat and oars; he greatly rescued the flood-tide; he gathered righteous troops and supported and upheld the royal house, sharing the state's weal and woe; twice he restored the realm within the Four Seas; now he receives the bright edict, assists my tender youth; manifest mandate arrives in glory, Heaven's majesty is within a foot's distance; facing and proclaiming the honored title, my grieving heart loses its design.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Marshal, the Duke of Tang, was born for the age and rose to lead the government—called the boat and oar of the realm, he rescued the nation from drowning waters, rallied the righteous armies, and upheld the imperial house, sharing its fortunes through good and ill and twice restoring order within the Four Seas. Now, bearing the bright edict, he assists my tender youth; his august commission shines upon us, Heaven's might is almost within reach. Facing him and accepting the honored title, my grieving heart knows no course.

sentences.zh: 一人在遠，三讓不遂，僶俛南面，厝身無所，苟利社稷，莫敢或違，俯從羣議，奉遵聖旨。

translations.literal: With one person far away, thrice I declined and could not succeed; bowing my head I face south, with no place to set my body; if it benefits the altars of soil and grain, I dare not disobey in any way; I humbly follow the multitude's counsel and respectfully obey the sacred intent.
translations.idiomatic: With one man still far away, thrice I declined and could not prevail; bowing low I take the south-facing throne with nowhere to rest myself. If the altars of state may benefit, I dare not refuse—humbly I follow the counsel of the assembly and obey the sacred command.

sentences.zh: 可大赦天下，改大業十三年為義寧元年。

translations.literal: A general amnesty for All Under Heaven is permitted; Daye thirteenth year is changed to Yining first year.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty is hereby granted throughout the realm, and the thirteenth year of Daye is renamed the first year of Yining.

sentences.zh: 十一月十六日昧爽以前，大辟罪已下，皆赦除之；

translations.literal: Before dawn on the sixteenth day of the eleventh month, for offenses from capital crimes downward, all are pardoned and remitted;
translations.idiomatic: Before dawn on the sixteenth day of the eleventh month, all offenses from capital crimes downward shall be pardoned and remitted;

sentences.zh: 常赦所不免者，不在赦限。

translations.literal: Those whom ordinary amnesties do not exempt are not within the scope of the pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Crimes ordinarily exempt from amnesty remain outside the scope of this pardon.

sentences.zh: 」甲子，以光祿大夫、大將軍、太尉唐公為假黃鉞、使持節、大都督內外諸軍事、尚書令、大丞相，進封唐王。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi, the Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Grand General, Grand Marshal Duke of Tang was made provisional bearer of the yellow battle-axe, commissioner holding credentials, Grand Commander of all military affairs at home and abroad, Director of the Department of State Affairs, Grand Chancellor, and was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day, the Duke of Tang—holding the posts of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Grand General, and Grand Marshal—was given provisional authority over the yellow battle-axe, commissioned with imperial credentials as Grand Commander of all military affairs at home and abroad, made Director of the Department of State Affairs and Grand Chancellor, and advanced to the rank of Prince of Tang.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，詔曰：「朕惟孺子，未出深宮，太上遠巡，追蹤穆滿。

translations.literal: On the day bingyin, an edict said: "I am but a child, never having left the deep palace; the Retired Emperor tours afar, tracing the tracks of Mu and Man."
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin day an edict proclaimed: "I am but a child who has never left the inner palace; the Retired Emperor roams far abroad, following in the footsteps of King Mu of Zhou."

sentences.zh: 時逢多難，委當尊極，辭不獲免，恭己臨朝，若涉大川，罔知所濟，撫躬永歎，憂心孔棘。

translations.literal: The times meet many difficulties; the supreme dignity is entrusted to me; declining, I cannot be exempted; reverently I hold myself and face court, as if crossing a great river, not knowing where to cross; stroking my person I sigh endlessly; my anxious heart is exceedingly troubled.
translations.idiomatic: In this age of many calamities the supreme dignity has been laid upon me; though I decline I cannot be spared. Reverently holding myself in check I preside over court, as one crossing a great river without knowing how to reach the other shore. I sigh endlessly in self-reproach, and my heart is sorely troubled.

sentences.zh: 民之情偽，曾未之聞，王業艱難，載云其易。

translations.literal: The people's truth and falsehood I have never yet heard of; the royal enterprise's hardship—they say it is easy!
translations.idiomatic: I have never yet learned the ways of the people, yet I am told the royal enterprise is an easy thing!

sentences.zh: 賴股肱戮力，上宰賢良，匡佐沖人，輔其不逮。

translations.literal: Relying on the limbs and trunks exerting their strength, the chief ministers wise and good, supporting and assisting the immature person, helping where I fall short.
translations.idiomatic: I rely on my ministers to exert their full strength, on wise and capable chief officials to support and counsel my youth and supply what I lack.

sentences.zh: 軍國機務，事無大小，文武設官，位無貴賤，憲章賞罰，咸歸相府，庶績其凝，責成斯屬，逖聽前史，茲為典故。

translations.literal: Military and state urgent affairs, matters without great or small; civil and military officials set in office, ranks without noble or base; statutes of reward and punishment—all return to the chancellor's office; may achievements be consolidated, responsibility fulfilled therein—hearing the former histories afar, this is established precedent.
translations.idiomatic: All affairs of army and state, great and small alike; the appointment of civil and military officials regardless of rank; the statutes of reward and punishment—all shall lie with the chancellor's office, that achievements may be consolidated and responsibility fulfilled there. Listening to the records of antiquity, this is established precedent.

sentences.zh: 因循仍舊，非曰徒言，所存至公，無為讓德。

translations.literal: Following precedent and continuing as before is not merely empty words; what is preserved is utter fairness, without pretense of yielding virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Continuing as before is no empty formula—the aim is utter fairness, not a show of yielding virtue.

sentences.zh: 」己巳，以唐王子隴西公建成為唐國世子，敦煌公為京兆尹，[2]改封秦公，元吉為齊公，食邑各萬戶。

translations.literal: On the day jisi, the Duke of Tang's son the Duke of Longxi Jiancheng was made Heir of the State of Tang; the Duke of Dunhuang was made Governor of Jingzhao, [2] changed in enfeoffment to Duke of Qin; Yuanji was made Duke of Qi; each received a fief of ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi day, the Duke of Tang's son, the Duke of Longxi (Jiancheng), was named heir to the State of Tang; the Duke of Dunhuang was appointed Governor of Jingzhao, [2] and re-enfeoffed as Duke of Qin; Yuanji was made Duke of Qi; each received a fief of ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 太原置鎮北府。

translations.literal: At Taiyuan the Northern Garrison Office was established.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Garrison Office was established at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，張掖康老和舉兵反。

translations.literal: On the day yihai, Kang Laohe of Zhangye raised troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai day, Kang Laohe of Zhangye raised an army in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 十二月癸未，薛舉自稱天子，寇扶風。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day guiwei, Xue Ju proclaimed himself Son of Heaven and invaded Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on guiwei day, Xue Ju declared himself emperor and attacked Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 秦公為元帥，擊破之。

translations.literal: The Duke of Qin served as supreme commander and crushed them.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Qin served as supreme commander and routed them.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，桂陽人曹武徹舉兵反，建元通聖。

translations.literal: On the day dinghai, Cao Wuche of Guiyang raised troops in rebellion and established the era name Tongsheng.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai day, Cao Wuche of Guiyang raised an army in rebellion and proclaimed the era Tongsheng.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，義師擒驍衞大將軍屈突通於閿鄉，虜其眾數萬。

translations.literal: On the day dingyou, the righteous army captured the Valiant Guard General Qutu Tong at Wen Township and took captive his forces numbering tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou day the volunteer army captured Valiant Guard General Qutu Tong at Wen Township and took tens of thousands of his troops prisoner.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，賊帥張善安陷廬江郡。

translations.literal: On the day yisi, the bandit chieftain Zhang Shan'an captured Lujiang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi day the rebel leader Zhang Shan'an took Lujiang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月丁未，詔唐王劍履上殿，入朝不趨，贊拜不名，加前後羽葆鼓吹。

translations.literal: In the second year, spring, first month, on the day dingwei, the Prince of Tang was permitted to wear sword and shoes in the hall, not to hasten when entering court, not to have his name spoken when praised in obeisance, and was granted feather-canopied escort trumpets fore and aft.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the second year, on dingwei day in the first month, the Prince of Tang was granted the privilege of wearing sword and shoes in the imperial hall, of walking at his own pace when attending court and of being addressed without his name in obeisance, and was given feather-canopied trumpets fore and aft.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，將軍王世充為李密所敗，河內通守孟善誼、武賁郎將王辯、楊威、劉長恭、梁德、董智通皆死之。

translations.literal: On the day renxu, General Wang Shichong was defeated by Li Mi; Meng Shanyi, Administrator-General of Henei, Brave Guard Lieutenants Wang Bian, Yang Wei, Liu Changgong, Liang De, and Dong Zhitong all died in the action.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu day General Wang Shichong was defeated by Li Mi; Meng Shanyi, Administrator-General of Henei, and the Brave Guard lieutenants Wang Bian, Yang Wei, Liu Changgong, Liang De, and Dong Zhitong all perished.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，[3]河陽郡尉獨孤武都降於李密。

translations.literal: On the day gengxu, [3] Dugu Wudu, Commandant of Heyang Commandery, surrendered to Li Mi.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu day, [3] Dugu Wudu, commandant of Heyang Commandery, surrendered to Li Mi.

sentences.zh: 三月丙辰，右屯衞將軍宇文化及殺太上皇於江都宮，右禦衞將軍獨孤盛死之。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day bingchen, Right Garrison Guard General Yuwen Huaji killed the Retired Emperor at the Jiangdu Palace; Right Imperial Guard General Dugu Sheng died in the event.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on bingchen day, Right Garrison Guard General Yuwen Huaji killed the Retired Emperor at the Jiangdu Palace; Right Imperial Guard General Dugu Sheng died defending him.

sentences.zh: 齊王暕，趙王杲，燕王倓，光祿大夫、開府儀同三司、行右翊衞大將軍宇文協，金紫光祿大夫、內史侍郎虞世基，銀青光祿大夫、御史大夫裴蘊，通議大夫、行給事郎許善心，皆遇害。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Yang Jian, Prince of Zhao Yang Gao, Prince of Yan Yang Dan, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Grand Master of the Palace with Honors Equal to the Three Lords and Acting General-in-Chief of the Right Wing Guard Yuwen Xie, Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Palace Secretary Yu Shiji, Grand Master of the Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon, Censor-in-Chief Pei Yun, Grand Master for Discussion of Affairs, Acting Recorder Xu Shansin—all met with violent death.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qi Yang Jian, Prince of Zhao Yang Gao, Prince of Yan Yang Dan, Yuwen Xie (Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and acting General-in-Chief of the Right Wing Guard), Yu Shiji (Palace Secretary), Pei Yun (Censor-in-Chief), and Xu Shansin (Acting Recorder)—all were killed.

sentences.zh: 化及立秦王浩為帝，自稱大丞相，朝士文武皆受其官爵。

translations.literal: Huaji installed Prince of Qin Yang Hao as emperor, styled himself Grand Chancellor, and all court civil and military officials received offices and ranks from him.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji enthroned Prince of Qin Yang Hao as emperor, styled himself Grand Chancellor, and all officials at court received appointments and titles from him.

sentences.zh: 光祿大夫、宿公麥才，折衝郎將、朝請大夫沈光，同謀討賊，夜襲化及營，反為所害。

translations.literal: Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Duke of Su Mai Cai, and Vanguard Lieutenant, Gentleman for Court Presentation Shen Guang, together plotted to strike down the rebels; by night they raided Huaji's camp and were in turn killed by him.
translations.idiomatic: Mai Cai, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Duke of Su, and Shen Guang, vanguard lieutenant and Gentleman for Court Presentation, plotted together to attack the rebels; by night they raided Huaji's camp but were killed in turn.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，詔唐王備九錫之禮，加璽紱、遠遊冠、綠綟綬，位在諸侯王上。

translations.literal: On the day wuchen, the Prince of Tang was granted the full Nine Bestowals; he was given the seal and ribbon, the Far-Traveling Cap, and the green cord and crimson sash; his rank was set above all feudal princes and kings.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen day the Prince of Tang was granted the full Nine Bestowals—seal and ribbon, Far-Traveling Cap, and green cord with crimson sash—and his rank was placed above all feudal princes.

sentences.zh: 唐國置丞相已下，一依舊式。

translations.literal: For the State of Tang, offices from Grand Chancellor downward were established entirely according to the old pattern.
translations.idiomatic: For the State of Tang, offices from Grand Chancellor downward were established entirely according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 五月乙巳朔，詔唐王冕十有二旒，建天子旌旗，出警入蹕，金根車駕，備五時副車，置旄頭雲罕車，儛八佾，設鍾虡宮懸。

translations.literal: On the first day of the fifth month, yisi, the Prince of Tang was granted a cap with twelve tassels, imperial standards and banners, outriders and imperial escort on entering and leaving, the golden-root chariot, five seasonal supplementary chariots, the Maotou and Yunhan war chariots, the eight rows of dancers, and palace bell and stone chime sets.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the fifth month (yisi), the Prince of Tang was granted a twelve-tasseled imperial cap, the emperor's banners and standards, outriders and imperial escort, the golden-root chariot with its five seasonal equipages, the Maotou and Yunhan chariots, eight rows of ritual dancers, and the full palace bell and stone chime ensemble.

sentences.zh: 王后、王子、王女爵命之號，一遵舊典。

translations.literal: Titles and designations for the prince's consort, sons, and daughters followed the old canon entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Titles and ranks for the prince's consort, sons, and daughters all followed the established canon.

sentences.zh: 戊午，詔曰：

translations.literal: On the day wuwu, an edict said:
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu day an edict proclaimed:

sentences.zh: 天禍隋國，大行太上皇遇盜江都，酷甚望夷，釁深驪北。

translations.literal: Heaven calamity befell the Sui state; the late Retired Emperor met robbers at Jiangdu—the cruelty exceeding Wangyi, the outrage deeper than north of Mount Li.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has calamitously struck the Sui state: the late Retired Emperor was murdered by bandits at Jiangdu—a cruelty surpassing the death at Wangyi, an outrage deeper than the killing at Mount Li.

sentences.zh: 憫予小子，奄逮丕愆，哀號承感，心情糜潰，仰惟荼毒，仇復靡申，形影相弔，罔知啟處。

translations.literal: Pity this child of mine—suddenly I meet great fault; wailing I receive the stirring; heart and feelings are crushed and broken; looking up I contemplate the bitter poison; vengeance cannot be declared; shadow and form mourn each other; I know not how to conduct myself.
translations.idiomatic: Pity this child of mine, suddenly burdened with grievous fault! Wailing I am seized by grief; my heart and spirit are shattered. Looking up at this bitter calamity, I have no way to fulfill revenge. Shadow and form mourn each other; I know not how to conduct myself.

sentences.zh: 相國唐王，膺期命世，扶危拯溺，自北徂南，東征西怨，總九合於一匡，決百勝於千里，糾率夷夏，大庇氓黎，保乂朕躬，繄王是賴。

translations.literal: Chancellor of State, Prince of Tang, receives the season and is fated for the age; he supports the endangered and rescues the drowning; from north to south, east in campaign and west with complaint—he gathers nine unite in one correction, decides a hundred victories within a thousand li; he assembles and leads barbarian and Han, greatly shelters the common people; he protects and comforts my person—in the prince alone I rely.
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellor of State, Prince of Tang, was born for the age, rescues the endangered and saves the drowning; from north to south, campaigning east while the west complains—he gathers the nine unite in one correction and decides a hundred victories across a thousand leagues; he rallies barbarian and Han alike and shelters the common people, protects and comforts my person—in him alone I rely.

sentences.zh: 德侔造化，功格蒼旻，兆庶歸心，曆數斯在，屈為人臣，載違天命。

translations.literal: His virtue equals creation and transformation; his merit reaches the azure heavens; the myriad people turn their hearts to him; the succession is here—yet bowing as a human subject, he constantly violates Heaven's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: His virtue equals that of Heaven and Earth, his merit reaches the azure skies; the people turn their hearts to him and the mandate of succession is his—yet he remains in subject's garb, defying Heaven's decree.

sentences.zh: 在昔虞、夏，揖讓相推，苟非重華，誰堪命禹！

translations.literal: In former times Yu and Xia yielded to one another in succession—if not for Chonghua, who could entrust the mandate to Yu!
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times Yu and Xia yielded the throne to one another—if not for Emperor Shun (Chonghua), who could have entrusted the mandate to Yu!

sentences.zh: 當今九服崩離，三靈改卜，大運去矣，請避賢路，兆謀布德，顧己莫能，私僮命駕，須歸藩國。

translations.literal: Now the nine domains crumble and scatter; the three spirits change their divination; the great fortune departs—I beg to yield the path to the worthy; the auspice is sought, virtue spread abroad; looking at myself, I am not capable; my private servants I order to prepare the carriage—I must return to my feudal state.
translations.idiomatic: Now the nine domains lie in ruin, the three spirits have changed their auguries, the great fortune has departed—I yield the path to the worthy. The auspices are cast and virtue proclaimed, yet looking upon myself I am not equal to the task. I have ordered my servants to prepare the carriage; I must return to my princely domain.

sentences.zh: 予本代王，及予而代，天之所廢，豈期如是！

translations.literal: I was originally Prince of Dai—"Dai" and "to replace"—what Heaven has cast aside, who could have expected it thus!
translations.idiomatic: I was originally Prince of Dai—and now "Dai" has become "replacement." What Heaven casts aside, who could have foreseen such an end!

sentences.zh: 庶憑稽古之聖，以誅四凶，幸值惟新之恩，預充三恪。

translations.literal: May I rely on the sage who examines antiquity to execute the Four Evils; fortunately meeting the grace of renewal, I am beforehand enrolled among the Three Reverences.
translations.idiomatic: May I rely on the sage who examines antiquity to punish the Four Evils; fortunate to receive the grace of the new dynasty, I may yet be counted among the Three Reverences.

sentences.zh: 雪寃恥於皇祖，守禋祀為孝孫，朝聞夕殞，及泉無恨，今遵故事，遜於舊邸。

translations.literal: To wipe away shame and disgrace for the imperial ancestor, to keep the ancestral sacrifices as a filial grandson—hearing in the morning and dying at evening, down to the Yellow Springs without regret; now following old precedent I yield at the former residence.
translations.idiomatic: To avenge the wrong done my imperial forebear, to keep the ancestral rites as a filial grandson—if I heard of it at dawn and died at dusk I would die without regret down to the Yellow Springs. Now following precedent I yield the throne at my former residence.

sentences.zh: 庶官羣辟，改事唐朝，宜依前典，趣上尊號。

translations.literal: All officials and the assembled lords: change your service to the Tang dynasty; you should according to former canon hasten to bestow the honored title.
translations.idiomatic: All officials and assembled lords: transfer your allegiance to the Tang dynasty; according to precedent, hasten to bestow the supreme title.

sentences.zh: 若釋重負，感泰兼懷，假手真人，俾除醜逆。

translations.literal: As if shedding a heavy burden; feeling both peace and gratitude; borrowing the hand of the true man, that he may remove the vile rebels.
translations.idiomatic: As if casting off a heavy burden, I feel both peace and gratitude—through the hand of the true sovereign, may the vile rebels be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 濟濟多士，明知朕意。

translations.literal: The multitude of worthy officers—clearly know my intent.
translations.idiomatic: You many officers—surely you understand my intent.

sentences.zh: 仍勑有司，凡有表奏，皆不得以聞。

translations.literal: Furthermore he ordered the responsible offices that all memorials and reports were not to be forwarded to him.
translations.idiomatic: He further instructed the responsible offices that all memorials and reports were not to be forwarded to him.

sentences.zh: 是日，上遜位於大唐，以為酅國公。

translations.literal: On that day, the emperor yielded the throne to Great Tang and was made Duke of Xi.
translations.idiomatic: On that day the emperor abdicated in favor of Great Tang and was enfeoffed as Duke of Xi.

sentences.zh: 武德二年夏五月崩，時年十五。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fifth month of the second year of Wude he died; at the time he was fifteen years of age.
translations.idiomatic: He died in summer of the fifth month of Wude year two, at the age of fifteen.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：恭帝年在幼沖，遭家多難，一人失德，四海土崩。

translations.literal: The historian states: Emperor Gong's years were in tender youth; he met the family in many difficulties; one man lost virtue, and the Four Seas' earth crumbled.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Emperor Gong was still in his tender youth when his house met calamity upon calamity—one man's loss of virtue brought the realm crumbling to ruin.

sentences.zh: 羣盜蜂起，豺狼塞路，南巢遂往，流彘不歸。

translations.literal: Bandits swarmed like bees; wolves and jackals blocked the roads; to South Nest they went forth, to Flowing Pig they did not return.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels swarmed like bees; wolves and jackals blocked every road—like King Jie they marched to South Nest, like King Li they never returned from exile.

sentences.zh: 既鍾百六之期，躬踐數終之運，謳歌有屬，笙鍾變響，雖欲不遵堯舜之迹，其庸可得乎！

translations.literal: Having already met the period of the hundred-six calamities, personally treading the fortune of exhausted numbering—songs of praise had their object, bells and flutes changed their sound; though one wished not to follow the traces of Yao and Shun, how could it be achieved!
translations.idiomatic: Having entered the era of cosmic calamity and personally tread the fortune of an exhausted mandate—the song of praise already had its object, the bells and flutes had changed their tune. Even had he wished not to follow in the footsteps of Yao and Shun, how could he have done otherwise!

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes

sentences.zh: 大業三年 據本書煬帝紀上、通鑑隋紀四，大業二年，侑封為代王。

translations.literal: Daye third year: According to the Annals of Emperor Yang 1 in this book and Comprehensive Mirror, Sui Annals 4, in Daye second year You was enfeoffed as Prince of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: [Regarding "Daye third year"]: According to the Annals of Emperor Yang 1 in this book and Comprehensive Mirror, Sui Annals 4, in Daye year two You was enfeoffed as Prince of Dai.

sentences.zh: 敦煌公 指李世民，時李世民封敦煌郡公。

translations.literal: Duke of Dunhuang: this refers to Li Shimin; at the time Li Shimin was enfeoffed as Duke of Dunhuang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Dunhuang: this refers to Li Shimin, who at the time held the title Duke of Dunhuang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 唐人因避諱缺其名。

translations.literal: Tang people, because of taboo avoidance, omitted his name.
translations.idiomatic: Tang-era editors omitted his name to avoid taboo.

sentences.zh: 庚戌 此月丁未朔，庚戌

translations.literal: Gengxu: This month dingwei is the new moon; gengxu
translations.idiomatic: [Regarding "gengxu"]: This month's new moon falls on dingwei; gengxu

translations.literal: should be on renxu
translations.idiomatic: should be on renxu

translations.literal: (the sixteenth day)
translations.idiomatic: (the sixteenth day)

sentences.zh: 前，紀文當有訛誤或顛倒。

translations.literal: before—the annal text surely has error or reversal.
translations.idiomatic: before—the annal text must contain an error or transposition.
